It was announced on Weibo on September 11, 2024. plainText:
Chasing the Moon (Chinese: Dànyuàn Mèng Chángjiǔ, transl. May Dreams Be Blessed with Longevity; Japanese: ポケモンたちと秋の月 Pokémon and the Autumn Moon) is an short based on the . It was announced on Weibo on September 11, 2024. It was released on Bilibili, Douyin, Weibo, and Xiaohongshu in on September 14, 2024, and on the official Japanese Pokémon Twitter account and YouTube channel and on the English Pokémon Kids TV YouTube channel on September 17, 2024.

==Other posters and logos==
 
Chasing the Moon poster.jpg|Simplified Chinese poster
Chasing the Moon poster 2.jpg|Simplified Chinese poster
Chasing the Moon logo.png|Simplified Chinese logo
 

==Blurb==
 
 The moon shines big and bright in the night sky. As Pikachu and the other Pokémon chase its glow, where could they be heading? Let’s find out. 

==Plot==
A stands atop a mountain, watching the scenery at twilight, when he notices the fleeting shadow of a soaring towards the horizon. Pikachu rubs his eyes in surprise and happily runs after Lunala. He loses sight of it upon reaching a pond and contemplates his reflection, saddened. Suddenly, a splashes the water when swinging over on a vine. Grookey lands gracefully and offers the soaked Pikachu a Pecha Berry. Pikachu gladly accepts it and eats it. As he munches on the berry, Grookey wipes the water off Pikachu's cheek. The two playfully nuzzle each other, and Grookey then knocks on the ground with his stick. Suddenly, a poised walks past them. The two decide to follow in its steps.

As Umbreon picks up the pace at a stone bridge-like formation, a pack of trails behind, followed by a . Grookey grabs onto Corviknight's leg and soars, but Pikachu fails to keep up. The Umbreon slows down again at a shallow lake and walks forward majestically. Many more Pokémon trail behind, most using paths of stepping stones on the sides. When Pikachu arrives, he encounters a large group of , who also begin to swim behind Umbreon. Corviknight finally lands, and Pikachu and Grookey reunite. Grookey leads the way across the lake, and Pikachu hops on the stepping stones behind the pack of Growlithe. Lunala's shadow appears over them once more.

Being the last Pokémon to cross the lake, Pikachu loses sight of the rest due to some fog, but soon finds them gathered near a cliff over a city. Lanterns illuminate the dusk sky, and a group of dance in a circle under the moon. Grookey swings over to Pikachu on a vine again, and everyone enjoys the view, with Lunala spreading out its wings in front of the moon.

==Trivia==
The short's Chinese title is a reference to the phrase dànyuàn rén chángjiǔ (may we all be blessed with longevity) from the poem by , which is associated with the Mid-Autumn Festival. It is also a pun on the Chinese name of Pokémon ( ).
The Japanese and Pokémon Kids TV uploads of this short do not contain ending credits, and instead end by fading to a black screen with a copyright notice.
The descriptions of the Simplified Chinese and Japanese uploads of this short mention that the short is based on the Mid-Autumn Festival. The description of the Pokémon Kids TV upload does not mention this.
The short is reported in 's "China Film Report" program.
